whatChanged: NEW: Procter & Gamble agrees to acquire science-backed supplements maker Thorne from L Catterton for $3.8bn in cash, its largest push into vitamins, minerals and supplements (pg-thorne-acquisition)

NEW: SpaceX and NVIDIA will jointly design the Starmind AI1 satellite compute payload, and Musk commits SpaceX to build its AI infrastructure exclusively on NVIDIA going forward (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership)

NEW: Netlist and Samsung Electronics sign a five-year patent cross-license settling all litigation -- $239m upfront plus up to ~$897m gross over the term, a $1.5bn memory supply line and a 10m-share equity purchase (nlst-samsung-license-alliance)
NEW: Axalta and AkzoNobel shareholders both approve the all-stock merger of equals at 0.6539 AkzoNobel shares per Axalta share, creating a ~$17bn-revenue coatings group (axta-akzonobel-merger)
NEW: AstraZeneca held early-stage talks with Bristol Myers Squibb about a combination valued at roughly $400bn, per the FT and Bloomberg; AstraZeneca shares fell 7% (azn-bmy-merger-talks)

themes.label: UK-listed franchises broken up or taken private
themes.note: London-listed names remain a magnet for control-changing bids from overseas and private capital: Prologis and Segro have agreed terms of a recommended Rule 2.7 acquisition valuing Segro at ~GBP14.3bn, which would remove one of the FTSE 100's largest REITs from the LSE (pld-sgro-takeover-bid), both easyJet suitors must declare a firm offer or walk away by August 7 with the board already agreed in principle to Apollo's ~GBP5.7bn terms (ezj-apollo-takeover), and CD&R-owned OCS Group's agreed GBP3.1bn takeover of facilities-management leader Mitie will delist another name entirely (ocs-mitie-acquisition). AstraZeneca's exploratory ~$400bn approach to Bristol Myers Squibb would move the pressure up to the very top of the index (azn-bmy-merger-talks).

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: PE-, sovereign- and strategic-led buyouts keep pulling listed names private: KKR has a signed $127-a-share, ~$5.7bn agreement for Integer Holdings (itgr-kkr-takeover) days after EA left the Nasdaq at $210 a share in the $55bn PIF-Silver Lake-Affinity take-private (ea-pif-consortium-take-private). Still live: Apollo and Castlelake both face an August 7 deadline on easyJet (ezj-apollo-takeover), Pacific Equity Partners' SG Fleet vehicle bids A$3.60 a share for FleetPartners (fpr-sgfleet-takeover-bid), Grant Thornton and New Mountain Capital's $5bn all-cash deal for CBIZ runs a go-shop to August 27 (cbz-grant-thornton-acquisition), Steel Partners' $16.75-a-share bid for InMode is fought through both the Haifa court and the AGM ballot (inmd-steel-partners-buyout), EQT keeps raising for Perpetual (ppt-eqt-takeover-bid), Frasers Group's EUR38-a-share tender for Hugo Boss is unconditional (boss-frasers-takeover-offer), Stripe and Advent's $53bn offer for PayPal remains live after board rejection (pypl-stripe-advent-takeover-bid), and Sazerac's revived ~$15bn approach for Brown-Forman has been rejected as not actionable (bfb-sazerac-takeover-bid).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital and commercial commitments keep pouring into the physical layer of AI compute, and the frontier has now moved off the planet: SpaceX and NVIDIA will co-design datacenter-class compute payloads for the Starmind AI1 satellite against an ambition of up to a million orbital nodes (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership). On the ground, Amazon's 2026 capex guide is raised to ~$220bn with capacity constrained into 2027 (amzn-capex-raise-2026) and Alphabet's to as much as $205bn (googl-capex-raise-2026), Nvidia is in talks to backstop ~$250bn of financing for OpenAI's 10GW Ohio campus (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop) and has an equity-plus-Vera-Rubin-capacity pact with Safe Superintelligence (nvda-ssi-partnership), the $10bn Naver AI factory scales to 200MW with Brookfield capital (naver-nvda-ai-factory-partnership), Orange and Morrison are building a EUR3bn, 400MW French data-centre JV (ora-morrison-datacenter-jv), Microsoft is deploying AMD's Helios systems at scale (msft-amd-helios-partnership), NVIDIA prepaid $1.5bn for packaging capacity at Amkor (amkr-nvidia-packaging-partnership), Verizon signed a $1bn dark-fiber deal with Google (vz-google-fiber-partnership), Samsung Electronics agreed a ~$200bn memory and foundry MOU with Broadcom (samsungelec-avgo-chip-partnership), SK hynix has a long-term HBM pact with NVIDIA behind a 2GW Vera Rubin AI factory (skhynix-nvda-ai-partnership), Everus bought modular mechanical and electrical specialist Epsilon Industries for $295m (ecg-epsilon-acquisition), Doosan took control of Korea's sole wafer maker SK Siltron for KRW2.3trn (doosan-sksiltron-acquisition), and Prysmian is paying ~$3.8bn for Atkore's conduit and cable-management business to sell into the same build-out (atkr-prysmian-acquisition).

themes.label: Chipmakers funding or locking in the customers that buy their chips
themes.note: Vendor financing and exclusivity are now the standard shape of frontier-AI deals, and both concentrate risk on the supplier's side of the trade: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee ~$250bn of lease and debt financing for OpenAI's Ohio campus (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), took a reported ~$5bn equity stake in pre-revenue Safe Superintelligence alongside a compute commitment (nvda-ssi-partnership), is buying ~4.5% of Naver via a ~$1bn share issue tied to a 200MW AI factory (naver-nvda-ai-factory-partnership), and has now secured an exclusive commitment from SpaceX to build its AI infrastructure on NVIDIA platforms (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership), while AMD is investing up to $5bn in Anthropic against a tens-of-billions MI450 purchase commitment (amd-anthropic-chip-partnership).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep drawing legal fire: the signed, DOJ-cleared Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger is formally paused by court stipulation until five days after an antitrust trial or June 1, 2027, with Paramount owing ~$7m a day if the pause runs past September 30, 2026 (psky-wbd-acquisition), while InMode's special committee remains procedurally frozen pending the Haifa court's ruling on the competing buyout bids, with the fight now also running through the AGM ballot (inmd-steel-partners-buyout).
